spec.name: News tone v13
spec.notes: Long names with improving news sentiment.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.0, annual return 3%, maximum drawdown 6%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.91 against 0.97 in research, a gap of +0.06.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.09, so the claimed 1.00 becomes 0.91 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.45 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.01, 95th percentile 0.54).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 0.97 to as low as 0.69 (as low as 0.76 at 25%).
Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 0.97 to 0.75 (change -0.22).

verdict.opinion: The strategy's Sharpe ratio is inflated due to selection bias. The best of 3 trials is expected to have a Sharpe of 0.09, but the claimed Sharpe of 1.0 is adjusted to 0.91. This suggests the performance may not be robust or replicable with real capital. Paper trading is recommended to further validate the strategy.
